implementation_notes: pact-js is the JavaScript realization: new PactV3({consumer, provider, dir}) declares the contract, the fluent given/uponReceiving/withRequest/willRespondWith chain declares one interaction, MatchersV3 (like, eachLike, term, integer, ...) keeps responses loose, and provider.executeTest(async (mockserver) => ...) starts the mock server, runs the client against mockserver.url and verifies the received requests when the callback returns. Provider verification lives in the same package (new Verifier({providerBaseUrl, pactUrls}).verifyProvider()), jest-pact and mocha-pact remove the fixture boilerplate, and Node 16+ is required from pact-js v12 on.
pitfalls: The mock only verifies what it receives: if the client never calls the endpoint, the failure appears when executeTest finishes, not inside the client code.
Node HTTP clients pool keep-alive sockets, so a connection reused from a previous test can point at a dead mock server and fail for reasons unrelated to the contract.
Calling the mock service with a raw fetch/axios request instead of the client under test passes the test while proving nothing about the consumer.
